blocks.prompt: 8. Use Trapezoidal Rule to approximate the value of the definite integral \(\int_{0}^{\pi} \sin(x^{2})\,dx\) taking \(h = \frac{\pi}{6}\).
blocks.explanation:
A numerical integration question: estimate a definite integral by the Trapezium Rule.
Given: \(f(x) = \sin(x^{2})\), interval \([0, \pi]\), \(h = \frac{\pi}{6}\), so \(n = \frac{b-a}{h}\).
Plan: list the points and 4-decimal function values, then use h/2 [first + 2(inner) + last].
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \sin(x^{2})\), \(a = 0\), \(b = \pi\), \(h = \frac{\pi}{6}\).
To find: an approximate value of \(\int_{0}^{\pi} \sin(x^{2})\,dx\).
Method: the Trapezium Rule, as the question asks. Here \(h\) is given, so find \(n\) first.

Continuity
\(\sin(x^{2})\) is a composition of the polynomial \(x^{2}\) and \(\sin\), both continuous, so it is continuous on \([0, \pi]\).
Why: the Trapezium Rule needs a continuous function on the interval.

Number of subintervals and points
\[n = \dfrac{b-a}{h} = \dfrac{\pi - 0}{\pi/6} = 6\]
Points \(x_{i} = a + ih\): \(0, \tfrac{\pi}{6}, \tfrac{\pi}{3}, \tfrac{\pi}{2}, \tfrac{2\pi}{3}, \tfrac{5\pi}{6}, \pi\)
Why: \(h = \frac{b-a}{n}\) rearranged gives \(n = \frac{b-a}{h}\); 6 subintervals give 7 points.

Function values (4 decimal places)
\[x_{i}^{2}:\ 0,\ 0.274156,\ 1.096623,\]
\[2.467401,\ 4.386491,\]
\[6.853892,\ 9.869604\]
\[f(0) = \sin(0.000000) = 0.0000\]
\[f(\tfrac{\pi}{6}) = \sin(0.274156) = 0.2707\]
\[f(\tfrac{\pi}{3}) = \sin(1.096623) = 0.8897\]
\[f(\tfrac{\pi}{2}) = \sin(2.467401) = 0.6243\]
\[f(\tfrac{2\pi}{3}) = \sin(4.386491) = -0.9474\]
\[f(\tfrac{5\pi}{6}) = \sin(6.853892) = 0.5402\]
\[f(\pi) = \sin(9.869604) = -0.4303\]
Why: First square \(x_{i}\) (a number in radians), then take the sine in radian mode. \(\sin(x^{2})\) is not \((\sin x)^{2}\). Two values are negative; keep their signs. The table with the answer collects them with their weights.

Add the inner values
\[S = f(x_{1}) + \dots + f(x_{5})\]
\[= 0.2707 + 0.8897 + 0.6243\]
\[- 0.9474 + 0.5402\]
\[= 1.3775\]
Why: these 5 inner values are shared by two neighbouring trapeziums, so they will be doubled.

Apply the Trapezium Rule
\[\int_{0}^{\pi} \sin(x^{2})\,dx\]
\[\approx \dfrac{h}{2}\big[f(x_{0}) + 2S + f(x_{6})\big]\]
\[= \dfrac{\pi}{12}\big[0 + 2(1.3775) + (-0.4303)\big]\]
\[= \dfrac{\pi}{12}(2.3247)\]
\[= 0.261799 \times 2.3247 = 0.6086\]
Why: \(\frac{h}{2} = \frac{\pi}{12} \approx 0.261799\); the end values are used once and the inner sum twice. Round only at the end.

Check:
\(\sin(x^{2})\) has no elementary antiderivative. A computer with very many subintervals gives 0.7727, so with only 6 strips the error is large (about 0.16): \(x^{2}\) runs from 0 to 9.87 radians, so the graph waves up and down faster and faster and 6 straight chords cannot follow it.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints 0.6179. Recomputing every ordinate gives the bracket \(2.3247\) and \(\frac{\pi}{12}(2.3247) = 0.6086\) (also 0.6086 with unrounded values). The correct answer is 0.6086.
